ui.coverage.text: French pilot: CTD notebook. Other operations remain in English.

ctd.intro.text: Read the water on the way down. On the way up the winch does not stop: close a bottle in as many layers as you can.

ctd.legendReview.text: Dashed: layers, in their channel colour. White dots: bottles.

ctd.legend.text: Independent channel scales · gaps remain gaps · white line: rosette

ctd.ready.text: {layers} layers in the notebook, {capacity} bottles on the rosette. Lower away; the winch holds at depth until you begin the ascent.

ctd.noLayers.text: No local cast offers two layers

ctd.retry.text: {error}. Close and reopen the CTD notebook to retry.

ctd.rules.text: A bottle counts toward the nearest layer it reaches: 100 at the layer, 0 at {limit} dbar error. Each layer keeps its best bottle.

ctd.recorded.text: Cast recorded; further casts are practice.

ctd.revealed.text: Layers revealed. Compare your bottles with the profile, or draw a new cast.

ctd.descending.text: Watch the curves emerge. Layer pressures stay hidden until recovery.

ctd.ascending.text: Hauling. Space closes a bottle; the winch does not stop.

ctd.atDepth.text: Downcast complete. Study all five curves, then begin the ascent when ready.

ctd.target.oxygen.rule.text: Find the lowest measured oxygen concentration.

ctd.target.oxygenMax.rule.text: Find the highest measured oxygen concentration.

ctd.target.pycnocline.rule.text: Find the strongest positive Sigma-t gradient with pressure.

crew6.instructions.text: Five pieces of clean suit are scattered through the container maze. Find them all, then get back to the rosette without touching anything: the ship is iron, zinc and copper from the keel up.

crew6.legend.brushing.text: Brushing along a surface keeps adding. Tia calls it at {threshold}.

crew6.reward.text: Up to 100 for a clean arrival · +40 for speed · +20 for a blank-grade run with no touch at all

crew6.status.start.text: Arrows or WASD to move. Hold a pad button or tap it for a short step.

crew6.meter.unsuited.text: Suit up first — the float coat can touch what it likes.

crew6.status.suited.text: Suited up in {time}. Back to the rosette now: every surface counts, so does the deckhand, so do the drips.

crew6.tia.detail.text: {count} touches: {surfaces}. Nobody wants a rusty blank.

crew6.tia.detailBrushing.text: {count} touches: {surfaces}, plus brushing along the way. Nobody wants a rusty blank.

crew6.status.busted.text: Tia: don't touch it, you're dirty. {count} touches. Change gloves and go again from where you suited up.

crew6.result.blankNote.text: Blank-grade: nothing on the bottles but seawater.

crew6.result.touchedNote.text: Tia logs what you brushed against the sample.

crew6.result.brushedNote.text: A few brushes on the way, noted on the sample sheet.

crew6.status.fresh.text: Fresh gloves from Tia. Back to the rosette from where you suited up.

early.closeRetry.text: Close and reopen to try again.

crew2.heading.text: Pick the old ice from the radar, then go prove it with an auger.

crew2.sceneLoaded.text: Scene loaded. Smooth and bright, or rough and bright? Mark your floes.

crew2.back.text: Back on the image. Add marks, then resume.

crew3.heading.text: Call the ice: first-year or multi-year, as fast as you can.

crew3.start.text: Level 1 waits on the surface. Press Space to start.

late.d692b6499cdd.text: A mast standing out of the ice, seen from a snowmobile, in the middle of the bay. The wreck sits upright near the centre of the box.

late.16bd7524fb9b.text: A small harbour; the GEBCO cell is land.

late.ab350b4c6c35.text: A small harbour; the GEBCO cell reads 2 m at the shore.

late.5939a44ddf0d.text: Abandoned in the pack beside the Resolute on Belcher's written order; the Resolute drifted a thousand miles east and was found afloat sixteen months later, the Intrepid was never seen again.

late.4315f0e18793.text: Abandoned off King William Island in April 1848, she was found in 2014 on the second survey line of a search box moved south after a davit pintle turned up on the shore, in the water Inuit had pointed to since 1869.

late.110310135da7.text: About 100 m (P:Breadalbane wreck site); the GEBCO cell gives 97 m.

late.9a5d94e14dad.text: About 11 m (P:Wilmot and Crampton Bay). The site lies just off the game's GEBCO grid.

late.e2c176e01de3.text: Approximate. The archive pins the loss off Cape Fry from Inuit testimony (E673); the artifact record pins it at Cape Searle because the wreck position is not fixed (A:wrecks-disasters-021).

late.82dce7f70367.text: Approximate: 'about 75 degrees 10 minutes north, 60 degrees 30 minutes west, some forty miles south of Cape York' (A:wrecks-disasters-017). No individual wreck has a fixed position; the named ships are listed in A:wrecks-disasters-044.

late.af16df5536ce.text: Approximate: the archive gives only Melville Bay (E1202).

late.4ba2f1ee0873.text: Approximate: the gazetteer pin off Cape Sabine (A:wrecks-disasters-005); the event record pins Kane Basin at 79.0 −71.0 and says 'position approximate' (E419).

late.4f3f1e2f0cd3.text: Approximate; the archive places the loss in Melville Bay (E680). McDougall's plate of the loss is pinned at 75.0 −64.0 (A:mcclure-investigator-073).

late.c8e54aa26fa9.text: Beach and shallows; the GEBCO cell straddles the inlet (254 m) and does not describe the shore.

late.9130ee2cd23e.text: Belcher's flagship, abandoned with the Pioneer in Wellington Channel with her colours nailed to the mast, 'as if we had encoffined some cherished object'.

late.e7bc5a73f543.text: Chartered to carry Garlington's party north to relieve Greely, she was nipped in Kane Basin and sank with most of her stores; the relief party's retreat left Greely's men to winter at Cape Sabine on almost nothing.

late.7fcf09ac095d.text: Crushed in Melville Bay on 23 June 1840 alongside the Bon Accord; the record says no more than that.

late.29a160837525.text: Driven ashore on Somerset Island in August 1825 and abandoned with her stores under canvas; seven years later those stores kept John Ross's Victory crew alive.

late.e7d8c142714b.text: Dundee whaler, earlier Peary's expedition ship

late.32306689fc0c.text: Fast in the harbour ice from 1830 and abandoned where she lay. Search the harbour itself, close under the shore, not the open coast outside it.

late.a65899e146fe.text: Frozen in at her winter berth inside a small, shoal harbour and abandoned there. The box is small; search close under the shore.

late.eed8facf059b.text: Her consort drifted east the length of Barrow Strait and Lancaster Sound. If the Intrepid went down near where she was left, she lies east of the abandonment position, down the drift.

late.acde809e77e2.text: Her engine useless from the first season, she spent four winters on the Boothia coast; on 29 May 1832 her colours were nailed to the mast and Ross went last over the side.

late.7761b2806807.text: In-nook-poo-zhee-jook pointed on McClintock's chart to the water just east of the north end of O'Reilly Island; the 2014 box was moved south to match the beach find. Search the eastern side, toward the peninsula.

late.0d383143b442.text: Kane's brig was frozen into Rensselaer Harbour for two winters; every man signed the paper to leave her, the flags were hoisted and hauled down, and the party walked once round the brig before setting off south by boat.

late.50a0261fbdec.text: Landing stores for Belcher's squadron with the Phoenix, she was nipped by a driving floe half a mile from Beechey Island and crushed in fifteen minutes; her people walked off onto the ice.

late.2a94fc553e15.text: Last seen 16 October 1835 drifting south in the pack; Inuit told Captain Harrison in 1840 that she was crushed off Cape Fry in December and that twenty-two sick men left ashore all died.

late.d78707d7d6c2.text: Last seen forty-five miles south-east of Cape Searle, drifting south in the pack, and crushed some weeks later. A ship crushed in a drifting pack goes down along the drift: look south of the datum.

late.fa0113f9ed6a.text: Leading a file of whalers and naval search ships through a crack in the ice she was nipped; two days later the repair was stove in and Belcher bought her for a hundred pounds for her oil and timber.

late.17301d97e9bb.text: Left at her winter berth in the bay with her colours flying. In 2010 side-scan sonar picked her up within fifteen minutes of the first line: she is close to where she was left, and the box is small.

late.8c23bf0b53a8.text: Left in the pack of Wellington Channel, which streams south into Barrow Strait. A ship crushed in that drift lies south of where she was left.

late.5e1e186ca40f.text: McClure took her into Mercy Bay in September 1851 and never got her out; after three winters and two scurvy deaths, Bedford Pim walked in over the ice and the crew abandoned her for the Resolute.

late.0737751829cd.text: Nipped about half a mile from the island, and found in 1980 upright in about 100 m half a mile south of it. Search the deep water south of the island, not the shallows under it.

late.7128b4ccf61d.text: Nipped in Smith Sound on 15 October 1872, she broke away from nineteen people left on a floe; the fourteen still aboard ran her into the land, wintered in a hut built from her, and the Tigress found her sunk the next August.

late.242f191241c8.text: Nipped in the pack north-east of Cape Sabine and gone in the afternoon; the party retreated south by boat. The pack in Kane Basin sets south toward Smith Sound: look south of the datum.

late.2f5867a9e905.text: Parry fixed the spot at 72°42′30″N 91°50′05″W. The ice drove her onto the beach, so whatever is left lies inshore, along the shore, not out in the inlet.

late.8afce8a29a0f.text: Parry's own fix, 72°42′30″N 91°50′05″W (E247). The hull broke up on the beach and nothing of it has been found since; the search is for what the ice pushed into the shallows.

late.2e392aa67fc4.text: Position from James Clark Ross's magnetic table (A:ross-victory-054). Never seen again after 1832.

late.b07b7467ca29.text: Rensselaer Harbour as pinned in the archive (E18). Never seen again.

late.1e13db7a0119.text: Run into the land at the cove and broken up by her people for a hut and a boat; the Tigress found her 'sunk about a mile and a half offshore'. Search offshore of the cove, to the west, out toward Littleton Island.

late.9aa69598240c.text: Sammy Kogvik of Uqsuqtuuq described a mast standing out of the ice in the bay; the Martin Bergmann turned aside, dropped a sonar and found a three-masted ship sitting upright in the middle of Terror Bay.

late.199455e62b1c.text: She was leading the file north through a crack toward Cape York when she was nipped, and went down in the same crack two days later. Look north of the datum, along the lead.

late.fc1d1fa8e360.text: The Carey Islands as pinned in the archive (E512). Which island she struck is not recorded.

late.79adaf70ef55.text: The abandonment position, 74°41′N 101°22′W (E1973). The ship drifted in the pack afterwards and was never seen again; where she went down is unknown.

late.3132dfc3cc67.text: The abandonment position, 75°31′14″N 92°21′55″W (A:wrecks-disasters-024). Never seen again.

late.a2a1daa1273e.text: The archive's Life Boat Cove pin opposite Littleton Island (P:Life Boat Cove). The Tigress logged the winter camp at 78°23′N 73°46′W (E168), a different longitude; the pin is used here.

late.4aef56028ce1.text: The archive's wreck-site pin (P:Wilmot and Crampton Bay); Parks Canada publishes a protected zone, not a position. Found 2 September 2014.

late.02a37eb98d68.text: The archive's wreck-site pin (P:Wreck of HMS Investigator); Parks Canada located her in July 2010.

late.db4ac4b976a8.text: The archive's wreck-site pin in the middle of the bay (P:Terror Bay). Found 3 September 2016.

late.2eaa942f661b.text: The cell at the pin; the islands' shoals run to the surface within 2 km.

late.464d69b04bbd.text: The cell at the pin; the neighbourhood runs from the shore to 210 m.

late.121e17a351d8.text: The fleet lay stem to stern against the land floe when the pack came in from seaward. The land ice, and Cape York, were to the north: the wrecks lie along the floe edge north of the datum.

late.cfe7a5c177e5.text: The record gives the bay and the date and nothing else. There is no clue to narrow the box; cover it.

late.22daef2b916b.text: The rounded position published for the protected wreck site (P:Breadalbane wreck site). Found by side-scan sonar on 13 August 1980.

late.3b8c9dd42d2b.text: The same Windward that carried Peary north in 1898, wrecked on the Carey Islands in June 1907; Captain Cooney and his crew sailed the boats to Pond Inlet.

late.3960315eef2a.text: The worst week the Davis Strait fishery ever had: a gale on 19 June 1830 drove the pack onto the fleet lying along the land floe, nineteen ships were crushed and a thousand men camped on the ice with no lives lost.

late.7e7d6f21b66f.text: Upright in about eleven metres, the upper deck about eight metres down (E894).

late.27766c23a9a9.text: Wrecked on the islands, not in the channel between them. A ship that strikes lies on the rocks she struck: search the shoal water against the shore, not the deep water offshore.

late.4209b38ebf9a.text: barque, Royal Navy (with her tender Pioneer)

late.4ba0202f9dba.text: one of nineteen or twenty whalers crushed together

late.b847dd9e6574.text: paddle steamer, John Ross's private expedition
